subject: Blended delivery SLA carveout request — streaming initial-burst expectations
messages:
From: Claire Simmons <claire@blueharbor.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@blueharbor.com
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: blended delivery SLA carveout for streaming POC

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo today — the throughput looks promising. We're planning a POC that mixes short interactive prompts (chat) and long-form generation (reports ~4–6k tokens). The product team flagged two constraints that will affect how we evaluate Redwood:

- We need a predictable "initial-burst" behavior for streaming endpoints: during some user flows the first token can be delayed while model warming and prefix decode happens. Can you provide a formal carveout or exception that explains how Redwood measures Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and what tolerances you can accept for a blended endpoint?
- Our SREs want a token/sec expectation for sustained generation (tokens/sec after first token) and a policy for sudden bursts (10–20 concurrent long jobs).

I've attached a short spreadsheet with our target SLAs and a rough call pattern. Can your team confirm what counts as a streaming vs synchronous endpoint for contractual purposes, and whether an explicit carveout for initial-burst behavior is plausible in a commercial agreement?

Appreciate a quick take — we need to lock evaluation criteria by next Wednesday.

Best,
Claire Simmons
Head of Platform Engineering
Blue Harbor Analytics

Attachment: blueharbor-streaming-sla-ask.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Claire Simmons <claire@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: blended delivery SLA carveout for streaming POC

Claire — thanks for the clear ask and for the doc. High level response while I loop in engineering and legal:

1) Definitions: for contracts we define two serving modes: "streaming" (server-sent incremental frames / chunked tokens) and "synchronous" (response returned when generation completes). Hybrid/blended endpoints are treated as streaming when they emit any incremental frames to the client.

2) TTFT carveout: we can provide an exception that documents a measured Time-to-First-Token window for blended endpoints. Practically, TTFT is influenced by model compile state, KV cache warmup, and the initial attention pass for long contexts. We typically measure TTFT p50/p95 across your workload profile and then agree an adjusted commitment for p95 during warmup windows.

3) Sustained token throughput: we can commit to a baseline tokens/sec per dedicated slot and specify a degraded tier for burst conditions. For POC we can provide empirical numbers (from your attachment) and a fallback policy — routing to a compatible quantized variant if sustained throughput dips.

I'm attaching an internal runbook excerpt that explains measurement methodology. Karthik — can you confirm the plausible numeric ranges for p95 TTFT and sustained tokens/sec for the models Blue Harbor wants to use? Marcus — can you weigh in on contractual language we should propose?

Next steps: Karthik to reply with numbers; Lauren (legal) and I will draft carveout language to include as an addendum to the MSA.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
pri_yom@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-ma-redlines-2027-06-14.pdf (PDF, redlines placeholder)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <pri_yom@redwood.com>, Claire Simmons <claire@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: blended delivery SLA carveout for streaming POC

Claire / team — technical details below, written for contract-readers and SREs. I'll keep it concise:

Measurement notes (applies to blended endpoints on our hosted product):
- TTFT definition: time from HTTP request arrival to emission of first byte of model-generated content (server send). Includes routing, model selection, and first-token decode.
- Warmup window: we observe a warmup period for long-context workloads (context > 8k tokens) where KV-cache population and attention planning can add 80–220ms to TTFT on p95 for the first request on a slot.

Typical numbers (estimated, per dedicated GPU profile using the models you asked about):
- p50 TTFT (warm cache): 30–55ms
- p95 TTFT (warm cache): 120–260ms
- p95 TTFT (cold/warmup request, blended long-context): 300–650ms (this is where carveout helps)
- Sustained token throughput (after first token): 130–320 tokens/sec per dedicated v100-equivalent slot depending on quantization and sequence length distribution.

Burst handling policy suggestion:
- For bursts (10–20 concurrent long jobs), commit to best-effort routing with transparent fallback to a quantized variant if sustained throughput for a slot drops below 80 tokens/sec. We can define a recovery window (e.g., 60s) and an escalation path if fallback is triggered more than 3x/hour.

Contract language we recommend (short form):
- "For blended streaming endpoints, Redwood measures TTFT over the customer's production-like prompt set. During slot warmup the parties agree a one-time carveout for p95 TTFT not to exceed [X] ms for a limited warmup period per slot. Sustained throughput expectations are expressed as an operational range and include documented fallback behavior to alternative model variants in capacity constraints."

I'll drop a short technical appendix with histograms after we run a quick simulation on Blue Harbor's sample calls. Marcus — can you flag any items that Legal must review?

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Attachment: (referenced: internal-runbook excerpt linked to Drive)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <pri_yom@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Claire Simmons <claire@blueharbor.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: blended delivery SLA carveout for streaming POC

Thanks all — quick legal housekeeping:

- We can include a limited carveout as an addendum to the Master Services Agreement. It should specify measurement window, the maximum number of warmup events per slot per day (we propose max 5/day), and an objective tie to the customer's provided prompt set.
- We will not commit to an absolute hard cap for cold-start TTFTs without production telemetry; instead we offer a "measured commitment": Redwood will measure p95 TTFT over the customer's production-like test set and commit to p95 <= [agreed value] outside warmup windows.
- Pricing implication: if fallback to quantized variants is used frequently (defined as > 10% of requests in a 1-hour window), we reserve the right to propose capacity changes or tiered billing for sustained burst usage.

I've attached a redline of our standard MSA with a proposed addendum clause. Priyom — please confirm whether Blue Harbor wants the carveout as a non-billable pilot concession or a contracted SLA change for the entire term.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-ma-redlines-2027-06-14.pdf (redline excerpt)

From: Claire Simmons <claire@blueharbor.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 15:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: blended delivery SLA carveout for streaming POC

Thanks for the fast turnaround — this is helpful. A few follow-ups:

- For the POC we agree to the measured-commitment approach. Please run the histogram/simulation on the sample calls I included and provide p50/p95 TTFT and tokens/sec ranges by EOD Wednesday.
- Warmup events: 5/day per slot is acceptable for the trial. We'll monitor and feed telemetry into your SRE dashboard.
- Pricing: for the POC we'd prefer the carveout as a non-billable pilot concession; if usage patterns stabilize we'll revisit billing.

I'll sign the addendum if you can produce the measurement results and the draft clause by Wednesday.

One more ask — can you add a short runbook paragraph for our on-call SREs describing how to recognize a "fallback to quantized variant" in logs (keywords, metric names)? That will help reduce time-to-detect.

Claire Simmons
Head of Platform Engineering
Blue Harbor Analytics
